title: Chebyshev Nodes: Roots of the n-th Chebyshev Polynomial
content: chebyshevNode n k = cos((2k+1)π/(2n)) for k = 0,...,n-1 are the Chebyshev nodes — the roots of the n-th Chebyshev polynomial T_n. They are optimal interpolation nodes in the minimax sense: among all choices of n nodes in [-1,1], Chebyshev nodes minimize the maximum error of polynomial interpolation for Lipschitz functions. chebyshevNode_mem_Icc proves they lie in [-1,1] using cos_le_one and neg_one_le_cos.

title: Chebyshev Nodes Are Distinct
content: chebyshevNodes_injective proves the n Chebyshev nodes are pairwise distinct, which is essential for the Lagrange interpolation operator to be well-defined (distinct denominators xₖ - xᵢ). The proof uses Real.strictAntiOn_cos: cosine is strictly decreasing on [0, π], and the arguments (2k+1)π/(2n) all lie in (0, π) with distinct values — so distinct indices k give distinct cosines.

title: Lagrange Interpolation Operator at Chebyshev Nodes
content: lagrangeBasis n nodes k x = ∏_{i≠k} (x-nodes(i))/(nodes(k)-nodes(i)) is the k-th Lagrange basis polynomial: the unique polynomial of degree n-1 that equals 1 at nodes(k) and 0 at all other nodes(i). lagrangeInterp n nodes f x = Σₖ f(nodes(k)) · ℓₖ(x) is the Lagrange interpolation polynomial — the unique polynomial of degree ≤ n-1 agreeing with f at all n nodes. chebyshevInterp specializes to Chebyshev nodes.

title: Limit Points of Sequences and Closed Set Theorem
content: IsLimitPoint seq y means y is approached infinitely often: for every ε > 0 and N, there exists n ≥ N with |seq(n) - y| < ε. This is exactly the definition of an accumulation point (or cluster point) of a sequence. limitPointSet seq = {y : IsLimitPoint seq y} collects all limit points. limitPointSet_isClosed proves that for bounded sequences, the limit point set is topologically closed: its complement is open because if y is not a limit point, all z within ε/2 of y are also not limit points (by the reverse triangle inequality).

title: Erdős 1941: Divergence at Rational Multiples of π
content: erdos_1941_divergence axiomatizes Erdős's 1941 result: for x = cos(pπ/q) with p, q odd positive integers, there exists a continuous f such that the Chebyshev interpolation values 𝓛ⁿf(x) diverge to +∞. This is the key partial result underlying the conjecture: it shows that limit points need not be finite (i.e., ∞ is achievable). The proof in Erdős's paper uses intricate estimates on the Lebesgue function for Chebyshev nodes at these special points.

title: Erdős Conjecture #1151: All Closed Sets Are Realizable as Limit Points
content: erdos_1151_conjecture axiomatizes the open problem: for any closed A ⊆ [-1,1] and any x ∈ [-1,1], there exists a continuous f such that limitPointSet(chebyshevInterpSeq f x) = A. This is the complete characterization: every closed subset of [-1,1] can appear as the set of limit points of Lagrange interpolation at Chebyshev nodes. The special cases derived below (singleton A = {y} → convergence; A = [-1,1] → density) are immediate corollaries. Vértesi (1999) lists this as Problem 2.41.
